description:
STAGE 1, written before reading the brief. MATERIAL: every frame is built from one element only - the axis-aligned-then-rotated SQUARE, drawn flat with no stroke, semi-transparent, in a strictly achromatic-to-cold-slate range (near-black ground around #16181a, mid slate-blues, pale bone/paper greys). No curves, no lines, no text, no gradients except those that emerge from stacked transparency. Everything is squares over black.

WHAT IT IS A PICTURE OF: two things at once, and the tension between them is the whole work. In the middle sits a radially symmetric MEDALLION - a rosette / mandala / snowflake built by rotating a cluster of overlapping translucent squares around the centre, six- to eight-fold, so the overlaps stack into a lacy star with a distinct core, a body and a scalloped outer edge. Around it, filling the rest of the frame to the edges, is a SCATTER FIELD of loose squares at many scales and many greys, tumbled at arbitrary angles, some large enough to be cropped by the frame, some the size of a few pixels. So: an ordered crystalline centre inside a disordered debris field. It reads as frost on glass, a rose window, a snowflake under a microscope, or a shattered mosaic reassembling itself.

WHAT THE TWELVE SHARE: identical vocabulary and identical staging. Every one of the twelve is centred, every one has the rosette at the middle of the frame, every one has the scatter around it, every one is greyscale-with-cold-tint on near-black, and every one is built from the same square. There is no doubt at all that they are one project.

HOW THEY DIFFER (256 sheet): mostly by DENSITY, SCALE and VALUE rather than by kind. 1203347 - large pale rosette, dark slate interior star, heavy scatter, ~60 percent coverage. 1243682 - crisp six-pointed star with fine internal detail, more black showing. 1283437 - smaller pale ring, dark slate core, big blocky scatter with several very dark squares. 1310661 - the cleanest: a pale ring around a large flat slate hexagon, sparse scatter, most black ground of the dense group. 1366079 - very heavy, big pale plates crowding the frame, rosette nearly lost in its own scatter. 1446330 - the outlier: almost EMPTY, tiny dim squares on black, the rosette barely present as a faint smudge; at a glance the frame looks unfinished or under-exposed. 1475115 - mid-slate, a large open ring/annulus, comparatively few pale notes, the most graphic of the set. 1561509 - small, dense, dark-speckled cluster at centre with a lot of empty black around it. 1733538 - slate rosette overlapped by pale plates, muddled. 1835793 - pale disc with a fine dark-blue snowflake sitting inside it. 1985692 - very pale, huge, nearly fills the frame, low internal contrast, almost a white-out. 1991107 - pale mass with a dark speckled core, also nearly frame-filling. So the twelve run a genuine range from near-empty (1446330) through balanced (1310661, 1243682) to over-full (1985692, 1991107), which is variation of amount more than variation of idea.

STATES (states sheets, seeds 1203347 / 1243682 / 1283437 / 1310661): NEUTRAL is the fullest and palest - the rosette is a continuous, cohesive pale mass with a solid interior. STRESS is unmistakable and is a genuine structural change, not a tint: the medallion FRACTURES. Its continuous body breaks into separated clusters, the core opens into a hole of black (1243682 stress has a literal black pinhole at dead centre; 1203347 stress loses its ring entirely and becomes six or seven detached knots of small squares with ground showing through), overall value drops toward slate, and the pale plates recede. 1310661 stress inverts: the pale ring is replaced by a large flat dark slate disc with a small pale star left at the centre. 1283437 stress goes soft and radial, a smeared dark burst with a dark centre dot. RECOVERY returns to something very close to neutral - pale, re-consolidated, closed - but not identical: 1203347 recovery has a fuller pale body and different core detail than its neutral; 1310661 recovery has a thicker ring and a darker interior. Crucially, the SURROUNDING SCATTER FIELD does not move between states - the same big squares sit in the same places in all three rows - so identity is anchored outside the medallion while the medallion carries the state.

AT 120px: the work survives, but unevenly. The rosette silhouette and the scatter read at browse size, and the twelve are still tellable apart by overall mass and by how much black is left - 1446330 (near-empty), 1985692 (white-out), 1991107 (pale with dark core), 1475115 and 1733538 (slate rings), 1561509 (small dark cluster) are each instantly identifiable. But the five densest pale ones - 1203347, 1243682, 1283437, 1310661, 1366079 - collapse toward one another at 120: all read as 'pale scalloped rosette on black with grey confetti', and their internal core detail, which is what distinguishes them at 256, is gone. On the state sheet at 120 the neutral-to-stress change is loud and obvious for all four seeds; the neutral-to-RECOVERY change is faint - 1243682 neutral and 1243682 recovery are close to interchangeable at that size, and 1203347 is nearly so.

ARTIFACTS I NOTICE: large scatter squares are cropped hard by the frame on all four sides in almost every seed (1203347, 1366079, 1985692 especially) - it reads as an intentional bleed rather than a mistake, but in 1985692 and 1991107 the pale mass touches the edge and the composition loses its ground. 1446330 is so sparse it reads as a rendering failure rather than a quiet token. In 1366079 and 1733538 the scatter squares overlap the medallion and muddle its outline. Fine dark speckles in the cores of 1835793, 1991107 and 1561509 are at the edge of resolution and turn to noise at 120.
